newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LANDSBERGIS DENIES RUMOURS ON C.BANK GOVERNOR.
newsitem.headline: LANDSBERGIS DENIES RUMOURS ON C.BANK GOVERNOR.

text.p: The chairman of Lithuania's parliament, Vytautas Landsbergis, denied on Wednesday speculation that the ruling Homeland Union Party was considering removing the governor of the Bank of Lithuania.
"I have not participated in any meeting where this question (the removal of the governor of the central bank) was discussed," Landsbergis told Reuters.

The business newspaper Verslo Zinios said on Wednesday that Landsbergis' recent criticism of the supervision policies of the central bank might be an opening shot in the battle to oust central bank governor Reinoldijus Sharkinas.
The country's independent television channel LNK also said on Tuesday that it appeared that the Homeland Union was considering a shake-up at the top of the central bank.
"I think this speculation has no grounds," Landsbergis said.
The governor of the Bank of Lithuania is appointed for a period of five years by the country's president, with a majority vote by parliament.
Sharkinas entered office in February 1996, after the December 1995 banking crisis swept Kazys Ratkevichius from office.
He previously held the post of finance minister.
